sources.label: VA Auditor of Public Accounts, Comparative Report of Local Government Revenues and Expenditures, FY 2025
VA Auditor of Public Accounts, comparative reports (history)
VA Department of Elections, receipts of Tazewell County's local candidates since 2023

notes: Actual results for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2025, as reported to the Auditor of Public Accounts from the locality's audited financial statements, not a budget.
Includes public schools (the school division's operations and school construction), shown as schools and left out of the services and overhead shares, as in Connecticut and Massachusetts.
Covers general government, capital projects, debt service (principal and interest) and enterprise activities such as water, sewer and electric utilities. Depreciation is left out.
Left out: borrowing ($0), non-revenue receipts ($258,707) and transfers between the locality's own funds.
Judicial administration (courts, the Commonwealth's attorney and clerks) and community development count as overhead.
Debt is gross debt at year end: bonds, Literary Fund loans, other long-term obligations and temporary loans, for general government and enterprise activities.

Political money counts contributions from businesses, unions and PACs to candidates for the governing body, school board and the constitutional offices, filed with the Department of Elections since 2023. Virginia allows business contributions. Individuals and party and candidate committees are not counted. Committees are placed by their filing address, so a few may be assigned to a neighbouring locality.
Transparency practices have not been checked yet, so they are not scored.

sources.label: VA Auditor of Public Accounts, Comparative Report of Local Government Revenues and Expenditures, FY 2025
VA Auditor of Public Accounts, comparative reports (history)

notes: Actual results for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2025, as reported to the Auditor of Public Accounts from the locality's audited financial statements, not a budget.
Towns sit inside counties, and town residents pay both. Tazewell County runs the schools and most other services, so the town's budget is small next to the county's.
Covers general government, capital projects, debt service (principal and interest) and enterprise activities such as water, sewer and electric utilities. Depreciation is left out.
Left out: borrowing ($2,500,000), non-revenue receipts ($411,032) and transfers between the locality's own funds.
Non-departmental spending and capital projects other than schools and roads ($1,718,433) are spread across departments in proportion to their size.
Judicial administration (courts, the Commonwealth's attorney and clerks) and community development count as overhead.
Debt is gross debt at year end: bonds, Literary Fund loans, other long-term obligations and temporary loans, for general government and enterprise activities.
Political money is not scored: no local candidate committee could be placed in this locality.
Transparency practices have not been checked yet, so they are not scored.
